VERDICT 1: REJECT
The first solution incorrectly calculates the time spent driving each vehicle by assuming the same time (800 hours) for both, when in fact the hybrid car's higher efficiency means less time spent driving. It also misinterprets the time-rate relationship.

VERDICT 2: REJECT
The second solution incorrectly calculates the time spent driving each vehicle. It also makes a calculation error in determining the gallons per mile for both vehicles.

VERDICT 3: ACCEPT
The third solution correctly calculates the time spent driving each vehicle using the formula distance = rate * time, then multiplies this by the fuel consumption rate (reciprocal of miles per gallon) to find the amount of gasoline used. It accurately determines the difference, concluding that Karla would have saved 48.125 gallons of gasoline.
